title: Fix golangci-lint-pr-hints test
body:
### What happened?

Looks like the golangci-lint-pr-hints linter was updated recently to put the feature gate comment ahead of the owner field in pkg/features/kube_features.go

All the feature gates in pkg/features/kube_features.go are ordered by the following comments:

	// owner: 
	// kep: 
	// alpha: 
	// beta: 
	//
       // Describe the feature gate
      <declare the feature gate> 
 
The new linter changes now requires that the comment describing the feature gate should even precede the owner comment line which goes against the structure followed by the entire file and this needs to be fixed

### What did you expect to happen?

Feature gates should be ordered as follows to maintain parity with the rest of pkg/features/kube_features.go

	// owner: 
	// kep: 
	// alpha: 
	// beta: 
	//
       // Describe the feature gate
      <declare the feature gate> 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Update/add new feature gate to pkg/features/kube_features.go

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
# paste output here
```

</details>

nodes.title: golangci-lint: tone down comment checking
nodes.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind failing-test

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

39df946c06 was meant to enable stricter comment checking only for cmd/kubeadm because the maintainers of that want that. However, the exclude rule didn't capture all possible error texts and therefore some checks were enabled across the entire code base.

The extended pattern is now based on the golangci-lint source code.

Also, the hint config didn't suppress any of these checks.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes #121660

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

I verified that https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116516 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121456 pass without issues, while errors in cmd/kubeadm are still caught.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
NONE
```

title: Dualstack Service endpoints are only from one IP family
body:
### What happened?

For a dualstack Service, its endpoints are only from one IP family.
```
	if len(svc.Spec.IPFamilies) > 0 {
		// controller is connected to an api-server that correctly sets IPFamilies
		ipFamily = svc.Spec.IPFamilies[0] // this works for headful and headless
```
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/endpoint/endpoints_controller.go#L207-L213

But from the enhancement doc, it should have endpoints of 2 IP families.
```
2 single-family endpoints per backend pod: Make no change to the [Kubernetes Endpoints API](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.10/#endpoints-v1-core). Treat each IPv4/IPv6 address as separate, distinct endpoints, and include each address in the comma-separated list of addresses in an 'Endpoints' API object.
```
```
Given a phased approach, the 2 single-family endpoint approach represents the least disruptive change. Services will select only the endpoints that match the spec.ipFamily defined in the Service.
```
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-network/563-dual-stack#endpoints

There's a gap between code and doc.

### What did you expect to happen?

Endpoints of 2 IP families should be in a Service's endpoints.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a dualstack cluster and create a dualstack Service.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

When we disable only the Score plugin then scheduler configuration will result in default preScorePlugins with 3 enabled [NodeResourcesFit, InterPodAffinity, TaintToleration]
And due to this change, the preScore for **InterPodAffinity** results in skip status  for some case (still not able to figured out what exactly it is), and  this might result in a panic for kube-scheduler.

```
-------- Line Number 982 framework.go [RunPreScorePlugins]----------
for _, pl := range f.preScorePlugins {
		logger := klog.LoggerWithName(logger, pl.Name())
		ctx := klog.NewContext(ctx, logger)
		status = f.runPreScorePlugin(ctx, pl, state, pod, nodes)
		if status.IsSkip() {
			skipPlugins.Insert(pl.Name())
			continue
		}
		if !status.IsSuccess() {
			return framework.AsStatus(fmt.Errorf("running PreScore plugin %q: %w", pl.Name(), status.AsError()))
		}
	}
state.SkipScorePlugins = skipPlugins
```

The numplugin variable turns out to be negative.  

```

// It also returns *Status, which is set to non-success if any of the plugins returns

}()
allNodePluginScores := make([]framework.NodePluginScores, len(nodes))
numPlugins := len(f.scorePlugins) - state.SkipScorePlugins.Len() <====================== L1018
plugins := make([]framework.ScorePlugin, 0, numPlugins). <====================== L1019
pluginToNodeScores := make(map[string]framework.NodeScoreList, numPlugins)
for _, pl := range f.scorePlugins {
if state.SkipScorePlugins.Has(pl.Name()) {
continue
}
plugins = append(plugins, pl)
pluginToNodeScores[pl.Name()] = make(framework.NodeScoreList, len(nodes))
}
```

> - some PreScore plugins which returned Skip, but are disabled in the Score extension point

Add one of the following kinds:

/kind feature

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
-->

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The root cause is we can randomly customize the preScore & Score plugins in the `KubeSchedulerConfiguration` so there maybe 0 score plugins but x prescore plugins, then as long as one prescore plugins returns **skip**, we'll panic as the cap is negative, reporting `panic: runtime error: makeslice: cap out of range`

```
numPlugins := len(f.scorePlugins) - state.SkipScorePlugins.Len()
```

The precise number of *numPlugins* should be **plugin in f.scorePlugins also in SkipScorePlugins**, then we will have to traverse these two slices for comparison, considering the plugin number will not large, so I pick the `len(f.scorePlugins)` instead.

This bug was introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115652, so it's a regression.


#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--

Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.

-->
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/121630

<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
```release-note
Fixed a regression since 1.27.0 in scheduler framework when running score plugins. 
The `skippedScorePlugins` number might be greater than `enabledScorePlugins`, 
so when initializing a slice the cap(len(enabledScorePlugins) - len(skippedScorePlugins)) is negative, 
which is not allowed. 
```

title: Invalid status reporting in StatefulSet during rolling update with partition (investigation)
body:
### What happened?

This is a follow up to investigate and potentially fix based on this comment: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120731#pullrequestreview-1689842503.

The values for `CurrentReplicas` and `UpdatedReplicas` in status fields are invalid. 

### What did you expect to happen?

Quoting the comment:

There's still issue of the mismatching statuses, as I explained in slack, but I'll also post here for visibility:

While testing this PR I found STS status isn't also fully correct, I started logging out full status right after each wait command and I'm seeing this:

```
// CurrentRevision is the only revision, and the CurrentReplicas matches Replicas, ie. 3
STEP: 1: Status v1.StatefulSetStatus{ObservedGeneration:1, Replicas:3, ReadyReplicas:3, CurrentReplicas:3, UpdatedReplicas:3, CurrentRevision:"ss2-7b6c9599d5", UpdateRevision:"ss2-7b6c9599d5", AvailableReplicas:3}
// after first update, with Partition=1, we need to update only 2 pods (1 and 2), but CurrentReplicas (ie. old) should be 0, UpdatedReplicas (ie. new) should be 2
STEP: 2: Status v1.StatefulSetStatus{ObservedGeneration:2, Replicas:3, ReadyReplicas:3, CurrentReplicas:2, UpdatedReplicas:0, CurrentRevision:"ss2-7b6c9599d5", UpdateRevision:"ss2-5459d8585b", AvailableReplicas:3}
// after the pod removal, we need to recreate the pod for CurrentRevision, so CurrentReplicas=1, and UpdatedReplicas=2
STEP: 3: Status v1.StatefulSetStatus{ObservedGeneration:2, Replicas:3, ReadyReplicas:3, CurrentReplicas:1, UpdatedReplicas:2, CurrentRevision:"ss2-7b6c9599d5", UpdateRevision:"ss2-5459d8585b", AvailableReplicas:3}
if one checks the descriptions we have in [our API]
```

(https://github.com/kubernetes/api/blob/b01b44926aa4920c8c8c008003e16316cf59ffda/apps/v1/types.go#L276-L296) we clearly are doing a bad job reflecting the actual changes happening to Current(Replicas|Revision) and Updated(Replicas|Revisions) such that they don't reflect the actual state of world, since the division between Current and Updated should be strictly tied to Partitions (as described in [the original proposal](https://github.com/kubernetes/design-proposals-archive/blob/main/apps/statefulset-update.md)).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run the e2e test with logging of the status: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120731#pullrequestreview-1689842503.

In proxy-mode=ipvs kube-proxy will assign _service addresses_, like loadBalancerIP's, to `kube-ipvs0`. From the description it looks like 10.1.36.40, 10.1.36.41 and 10.1.32.40 are _both_ node-addresses and loadBalancerIP's.

Then you will get the problem you describe. It is mentioned in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114815#issuecomment-1382090138.

/area kube-proxy
/area ipvs

@uablrek this addresses are externalIps in the ingress service(type is NodePort).


![Image20231019160951](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/5180093/e0a685f7-8329-49b2-a8b8-27a9273be443)
externalIP and loadBalancerIP in services are manages in the same way. So read the above as loadBalancerIP==externalIP.
Try to simply remove `externalIPs` from the services

@uablrek Should I use nodePort instead of externalIps? in my case 32468 and 32402 ports? 
Are there any plans to fix it at all?

> Is there any plans to fix it at all?

No, it's just how ipvs works. You _must_ assign a load-balancer address to a local interface (any interface), and in K8s the dummy interface `kube.ipvs0` is used. But...

If the loadBalancerIP (or externalIP) is a node address, you get the conflict described in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114815#issuecomment-1382090138. Simply put, several machines in the cluster thinks that it owns the address.

But, I can't any reason to use `externalIPs` at all, and especially not to use a node-ip for them. It may be that some one thinks that `externalIPs` are just informative (like `spec.loadBalancerIP` in a service). But they causes the problematic config you see.

BTW, `externalIPs` is an ancient construct and has been proposed to be deprecated several times.
I have wished _so many times_ that a iptables target like `-j IPVS` existed, so we could skip `kube-ipvs0` altogether, but it doesn't :cry:
thanks for the help, have a nice day!

title: [KCCM]: service controller predicates might impact ingress SLO on GCP with InstanceGroup based Load Balancing
body:
### What happened?

In 1.26 the service controller in the Kubernetes cloud controller manage (KCCM) introduced a new mechanism for syncing load balancers based on predicates. The predicates applied will depend on "service classes", specifically if it's `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` or `Cluster`, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.26/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L944-L947

This implementation is not well suited for internal GCP load balancers which use InstanceGroups. @People from Google, feel free to correct me: any cluster has all nodes grouped together into an instance group. Service of `type: LoadBalancer` have individual GCP load balancers, but these load balancers end up referencing the same instance group (which is the cluster's instance group). This means that the inclusion/exclusion predicates for any service, will trickle down and impact the cluster's global instance group, thereby impacting other services which don't necessarily apply the same set of predicates. Ex: `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` services exclude `NotReady` nodes, whereas `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` do not. A Node going `NotReady` will therefore be removed from all backends for `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` services, however on GCP with load balancer solution based on InstanceGroups: this means that the same node will be removed from all backends for `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` services too.    

This is NOT a problem on >= 1.27 using the feature `StableLoadBalancerNodeSet`, because all services on 1.27 using that feature gate will have the same set of predicates. 

### What did you expect to happen?

Node updates requiring the removal of the instance from load balancers belonging to services of `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` should not impact other services of `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Bring up a cluster using "Internal load balancers" on GCP. Define two services, one being `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` and the other `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`. Have one node go `NotReady`. The instance corresponding to that Node might be removed from the InstanceGroup backend of the `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` service. This will depend on the order the services are synced, if the `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` service is synced last then the instance will be removed.  

### Anything else we need to know?

This is actually not really _that_ bad, because the only different predicate between both is the readiness condition - and a node should go back to `Ready` if all is fine, and finally be included. But I wanted to raise this for issue for completeness sake so that it is known. 

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
1.26 only or >= 1.27 with the feature gate `StableLoadBalancerNodeSet` switched off
```

</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>
GCP
</details>


### OS version

<details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
# paste output here
$ uname -a
```

title: [KCCM]: handle coalesced node updates in the service controller
body:
### What happened?

On big clusters with a lot of churn, Node updates can be frequent. The service controller in the Kubernetes cloud controller manager (KCCM) uses an edge-triggered resource watcher for what concerns handling the Update events, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L160-L176

This means that Node events which should trigger a sync (ex: the addition/removal of the label `exclude-from-load-balancer`) can be missed if multiple updates occur on the same object in a short amount of time. 

The `UpdateFunc` doc bloc even explicitly warns about patterns such as the one described above, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/controller.go#L207-L212

This pattern has always been used in the KCCM, but I believe that since some Node conditions which used to trigger re-syncs have been removed since 1.26, the error can be triggered more often now. Specifically on < 1.26, the `NotReady` condition on the Node used to trigger a re-sync. This condition usually occurs when the Node stabilizes, sometime after its initial creation. This covered the existing issue.    

/sig network
/sig cloud-provider
/cc @aojea @thockin 


### What did you expect to happen?

All Node events should get enqueued. The Node controller will compare the current set of nodes in its informer cache to the last set of Nodes it synced, if a change is observed the load balancer is synced, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L746-L751 - this shouldn't even lead to additional syncs because of this.  

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This can be observed on upgrading clusters with a lot of Nodes and Services of `type: LoadBalancer`. Some Nodes might get excluded from the load balancer's backend, not because they should be excluded but because the update which should include it is missed.

title: kube-proxy SNAT policy for nodeport should only be performed on traffic originating from the pod on the current host
body:
### What happened?

Pod A runs on host node-1, where there are multiple network cards (eth0:10.10.11.1, eth1:192.168.10.11). Pod A is associated with service A, which is a nodeport type and provides a nodeport 30001; Pod B runs on host node-2, and accesses Pod A through 192.168.10.11:30001. At this time, the source IP obtained inside Pod A is the IP of eth0 on node-1, and the expected IP is eth1.

### What did you expect to happen?


The source IP should be displayed as the IP of the network card through which the traffic actually passes. Some gateway applications require the setting of an x-forwarded for request header, which may be used in security policies. When multiple network cards exist, it is necessary to set the x-forwarded for to the correct business network card IP address.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

create nginx pod and config x-forward-for header，access nginx using pod host ip and service nodeport。

### Anything else we need to know?

kube-proxy add this rule for nodeport traffic:
-A KUBE-POSTROUTING -m comment --comment "kubernetes service traffic requiring SNAT" -j MASQUERADE

MASQUERADE rule will change the source ip to the network card with the highest priority on the host.

### Kubernetes version

/sig network

> MASQUERADE rule will change the source ip to the network card with the highest priority on the host.

This is not correct. First, there is no "highest priority" nic, and MASQUERADE sets src to the address of the _outgoing_ interface.

The src address you see is from K8s load-balancing and is as intended. If you need to preserve the original source address, you must use [externalTrafficPolicy: local](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tutorials/services/source-ip/#source-ip-for-services-with-type-nodeport).

It is also _highly_ dependent on the CNI-plugin. In your case you see a node-ip as source as I understand from the description. This is likely _not_ the case if the CNI-plugin uses a network overlay (as most do).

From kernel code: https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/94f6f0550c625fab1f373bb86a6669b45e9748b3/net/ipv4/devinet.c#L1345

netfilter doesn't like an address that is secondary, and like an address whose scope is global. Can you use `ip a` show the interface's address on your node?

![aaa](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/7565495/8043e6bc-5399-4091-a273-5d95f0c02319)

client conn: 10.10.11.12:30001 (30001 is the nodeport of service, and pod 127.16.1.2 is the endpoints of this service);
Expected source IP in pod is 10.10.11.12

I think it's caused by the rule add by kube-proxy：
-A KUBE-POSTROUTING -m comment --comment "kubernetes service traffic requiring SNAT" -j MASQUERADE

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When PodSchedulingContext or ResourceClaim is being synchronized in DynamicResourceAllocation helper code, it calls resource driver to get parameters for ResourceClaim and ResourceClass.

This PR introduces additional events for ResourceClass, ResourceClaim and Pod.

Additional events introduced:

- In ResourceClaim sync loop
  - if GetClassParameters call fails
    - send event to ResourceClass with error reported from Resource Driver
- in PodSchedulingContext sync loop
  - if GetClassParameters call fails
    - send event to ResourceClass with error reported from Resource Driver
    - send event to Pod with error reported from Resource Driver
  - if GetClaimParameters call fails
    - send event to ResourceClaim with error reported from Resource Driver
    - send event to Pod with error reported from Resource Driver

Example of ResourceClass event posted:

### What did you expect to happen?

we expect the kube-controller-manage will work well.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The following example can reproduce this problem:
```
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nginx
  labels:
    app: nginx
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 80
    name: web
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: nginx
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  serviceName: "nginx"
  replicas: 100
  podManagementPolicy: Parallel
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
          name: web
        volumeMounts:
        - name: www
          mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: www
      labels:
        a: b
    spec:
      accessModes: [ "ReadWriteOnce" ]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 1Gi
```

### Anything else we need to know?

After digging into the source code, we found that when using the `Parallel` pod management policy, the statefulset controller will use `slowStartBatch` to start parallel processing.
But the `getPersistentVolumeClaims` which is called during parallel processing may directly update the claims' labels without a lock. This finally causes a concurrent map-accessing problem.

I ran this test on `v1.27.3` (before the cherry-pick of parallel statefulset scaling), and it also failed. This is because the test itself introduces a concurrent map write. It probably doesn't replicate the issue, and I don't think it can be merged, as it'll fail even if the original PR is reverted.

For reproduction we'd need to catch a concurrent write without adding one in test code, just as it happened based on the original report.

Turns out we never tested this path at all, since the test PVC didn't have any labels of its own. After adding labels, existing tests are sufficient to detect race condition.

title: kube-proxy fails to start for IPv6 when underlying infra is dual stack in 1.28
body:
### What happened?

A new  kube-proxyvalidation introduced in k8s 1.28 seems to break Azure + ipv6. IPv6 clusters on Azure run on dual-stack hosts. The IPv6 node IP seems like it's only getting assigned to the Node until after kube-proxy starts (someone might need to help me understand what component is responsible). However, kube-proxy now fails to start with:

kube-proxy is in CrashloopBackoff, logs show:

``` 
I0825 16:18:19.872382       1 server_others.go:69] "Using iptables proxy"
I0825 16:18:19.892673       1 node.go:141] Successfully retrieved node IP: 10.1.0.6
I0825 16:18:19.894163       1 conntrack.go:52] "Setting nf_conntrack_max" nfConntrackMax=131072
I0825 16:18:19.912200       1 server.go:632] "kube-proxy running in dual-stack mode" primary ipFamily="IPv4"
E0825 16:18:19.912228       1 server.go:537] "Error running ProxyServer" err="kube-proxy configuration is incorrect: cluster is IPv4-primary but clusterCIDRs contains only IPv6 addresses"
E0825 16:18:19.912240       1 run.go:74] "command failed" err="kube-proxy configuration is incorrect: cluster is IPv4-primary but clusterCIDRs contains only IPv6 addresses"
```

Full logs: https://gcsweb.k8s.io/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/kubernetes-sigs_cluster-api-provider-azure/4086/pull-cluster-api-provider-azure-conformance-ipv6-with-ci-artifacts/1709361655076360192/artifacts/clusters/capz-conf-klo2dh/

### What did you expect to happen?

Kube-proxy should start. This does not repro with prior versions of k8s (1.27 and below). 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Build a Kubernetes cluster with v1.28 on Azure (underlying subnet has both IPv6 and Ipv4 addresses) with Kubeadm (e.g. CAPZ), configure the cluster CIDRs to single stack IPv6 (detailed instructions in https://capz.sigs.k8s.io/topics/ipv6)
- Observe the kube-proxy pod is crashing

This repros consistently

### Anything else we need to know?

This new validation was introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119003

### Kubernetes version

v1.28.0 and above


### Cloud provider

Azure

### OS version

Linux version 6.2.0-1011-azure

### Install tools

CAPZ

revision=b69f1ad231b6d87eeb30504398075a92d615e83e version=v1.6.23

### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

Calico CNI (Calico fails to start due to crashing kube-proxy)

>     E0825 16:18:19.912240       1 run.go:74] "command failed" err="kube-proxy configuration is incorrect: cluster is IPv4-primary but clusterCIDRs contains only IPv6 addresses"

do you have examples of the equivalent (working) startup logs from 1.27?

> The IPv6 node IP seems like it's only getting assigned to the Node until after kube-proxy starts (someone might need to help me understand what component is responsible).

There are two possibilities here:
- On first startup, kubelet detects the node IPs itself, so if the host hasn't completed IPv6 configuration yet, then kubelet will start up thinking that the node is single-stack IPv4 and set the Node object accordingly. #120751 will make kubelet not do this (cc @aojea), and instead rely on the cloud-provider to set the addresses, but also this is kind of a bad setup anyway; if possible, you should try to make sure that kubelet doesn't start until after IPv6 configuration has completed. (I'm not sure what sort of distro you're using, but if it's using NetworkManager, you just need to configure the default connection to have the "require IPv6 addressing" setting.)
- After first startup, the node IP should have been set by the cloud provider, so if the cloud provider doesn't know about the IPv6 IPs, then it still might be missing... that... probably shouldn't happen? But maybe the cloud-provider refuses to return the IPv6 IP until it has been configured on the node's NIC, in which case this is the same as the other case, and you should try to configure it to wait for IPv6 addressing to complete.

But anyway, yes, it looks like there was a regression: in 1.27, kube-proxy would limp through this problem but in 1.28 it won't.

nodes.title: Make a certain ipv4-vs-ipv6 config error non-fatal, for backward compat
nodes.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug
/kind regression
/sig network
/priority important-soon

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
kube-proxy historically allowed badly-mismatched bits of configuration (e.g., specifying an IPv6 `--cluster-cidr` value on a seemingly dual-stack-IPv4-primary node). In 1.28 I consolidated the existing checks and added a bunch more, but I accidentally made one case fatal which had not been fatal in prior releases. This makes it just a warning again.

(It is still fatal to specify an IPv6 `--cluster-cidr` on a _necessarily_ single-stack-IPv4 node (e.g., when kernel IPv6 is disabled).)

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes #120999

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Fixed a regression in kube-proxy where it might refuse to start if given
single-stack IPv6 configuration options on a node that has both IPv4 and
IPv6 IPs.
```

title: ServiceAccount not garbage collected when owned by another resource
body:
### What happened?

A ServiceAccount with `.metadata.ownerReferences` set to another resource (tested with ServiceAccount, Service, Deployment, ConfigMap and Secret) get not garbage collected when the owner resource is removed.

### What did you expect to happen?

The owned ServiceAccount to be removed when the owner resource get removed.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Here is a script to reproduce the issue:

```
#!/bin/sh

NAMESPACE=default
OWNER_KIND=Service
OWNED_KIND=ServiceAccount
CONTROLLER=true
BLOCK_OWNER_DELETION=true

get_apiversion() {
  echo "$(
    { kubectl explain "$1" | grep '^GROUP:' | tr -d ' ' | cut -d : -f 2 && printf /; } | tr -d '\n'
    )$(
    kubectl explain "$1" | grep '^VERSION:' | tr -d ' ' | cut -d : -f 2
    )"
}

get_kind_payload() {
  case "$1" in
    ('Service'):
      echo "
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 8080
"
    ;;
    ('Deployment'):
      echo "
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      test: test
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        test: test
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: test
        image: alpine
        command: [ sleep, '3600' ]
"
    ;;
  esac
}

OWNER_APIVERSION="$(get_apiversion "$OWNER_KIND")"
OWNED_APIVERSION="$(get_apiversion "$OWNED_KIND")"
OWNER_KIND_PAYLOAD="$(get_kind_payload "$OWNER_KIND")"
OWNED_KIND_PAYLOAD="$(get_kind_payload "$OWNED_KIND")"

kubectl delete --ignore-not-found -n "$NAMESPACE" "$OWNER_KIND" owner
kubectl delete --ignore-not-found -n "$NAMESPACE" "$OWNED_KIND" owned

echo

echo "* Creating resource $OWNER_KIND owner"

echo

cat << EOF > /tmp/owner.yaml
apiVersion: $OWNER_APIVERSION
kind: $OWNER_KIND
metadata:
  name: owner
$OWNER_KIND_PAYLOAD
EOF

kubectl create -n "$NAMESPACE" -f /tmp/owner.yaml -o yaml

echo

echo "* Creating resource $OWNED_KIND owned"

echo

cat << EOF > /tmp/owned.yaml
apiVersion: $OWNED_APIVERSION
kind: $OWNED_KIND
metadata:
  name: owned
  ownerReferences:
  - $(kubectl get -n "$NAMESPACE" "$OWNER_KIND" owner -o json | jq -c "{ apiVersion: .apiVersion, kind: .kind, name: \"owner\", uid: .metadata.uid, controller: $CONTROLLER, blockOwnerDeletion: $BLOCK_OWNER_DELETION }")
$OWNED_KIND_PAYLOAD
EOF

kubectl create -n "$NAMESPACE" -f /tmp/owned.yaml -o yaml

echo

echo "* Listing resources"

echo

kubectl get -n "$NAMESPACE" "$OWNER_KIND"

echo

kubectl get -n "$NAMESPACE" "$OWNED_KIND"

echo

echo "* Delete $OWNER_KIND owner waiting for deletion of child resources"

echo

kubectl delete -n "$NAMESPACE" "$OWNER_KIND" owner --wait

echo

echo "* Waiting for deletion of $OWNED_KIND owned"

echo

kubectl wait --for delete --timeout 10s -n "$NAMESPACE" "$OWNED_KIND" owned -o name

echo

echo "* Listing resources"

echo

kubectl get -n "$NAMESPACE" "$OWNER_KIND"

echo

kubectl get -n "$NAMESPACE" "$OWNED_KIND"

echo

echo "Cleanup"

echo

kubectl delete --ignore-not-found -n "$NAMESPACE" "$OWNED_KIND" owned
```

title: Fixes in cel-go breaks backward compatible of CRD validation rules between 1.27 and 1.28 release
body:
### What happened?

We were using cel-go v0.12.7 in Kubernetes 1.27 release and cel-go v0.16.0 in Kubernetes 1.28 release. There are many changes from cel-go side between those two releases and some may break backward compatible of CRD validation rules.

An example would be the estimated cost for CRD validation rules(Thanks to @inteon who brought this to our attention with the following example).
In the example CRD validation rules below:
```
---
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: resources.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  names:
    kind: Resource
    listKind: ResourceList
    plural: resources
    singular: resource
  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
  - name: v1alpha1
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        properties:
          apiVersion:
            type: string
          kind:
            type: string
          metadata:
            type: object
          spec:
            items:
              properties:
                a:
                  type: string
                b:
                  type: string
                c:
                  type: string
                d:
                  type: string
                e:
                  type: string
                f:
                  type: string
              type: object
              x-kubernetes-validations:
              - message: must have exactly one field set
                rule: '(has(self.a) ? 1 : 0) + (has(self.b) ? 1 : 0) + (has(self.c)
                  ? 1 : 0) + (has(self.d) ? 1 : 0) + (has(self.e) ? 1 : 0)
                  + (has(self.f) ? 1 : 0) == 1'
            type: array
        type: object
    served: true
    storage: true
    ...
```
It will pass perfect in Kubernetes 1.27 version but fail in Kubernetes 1.28 with error:
`Forbidden: estimated rule cost exceeds budget by factor of 1.6x (try simplifying the rule, or adding maxItems, maxProperties, and maxLength where arrays, maps, and strings are declared) `

This is due to the estimator fix happened in cel-go([cel fix 1](https://github.com/google/cel-go/pull/651), [cel fix 2](https://github.com/google/cel-go/pull/798))

### What did you expect to happen?

The changes should not cause backward incompatible of CRD validation rules. OR a stability test suite should be in place to prevent the changes causing backward compatible issue before GA.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Apply the above CRD in Kubernetes 1.27 and 1.28, 1.27 cluster should pass and 1.28 cluster should fail.

### Anything else we need to know?

Since the fix in cel-go side makes sense to me and the feature is in Beta now, I am not quite sure how strict we should be on backward compatible.  cc @liggitt 

As a followup, a stability test suite for estimate cost is worth adding before GA to make sure any future changes be caught before the feature promoted to GA.

```console
$ kubectl version
```

Hi @cici37, I agree that the changes in cel-go should not break the backward compatibility of CRD validation rules, especially for users who have already defined and deployed their custom resources using the previous version of Kubernetes. 

One suggestion I have is to use a **version flag** for the CEL library, so that users can specify which version of cel-go they want to use for their CRD validation rules. This way, they can avoid unexpected errors or behavior changes when upgrading their Kubernetes cluster. For example, they can add something like `x-kubernetes-cel-version: v0.12.7` in their CRD schema to indicate that they want to use the old version of cel-go.

Another suggestion I have is to use a **cost limit** parameter for the CEL library, so that users can adjust the budget for their CRD validation rules. This way, they can fine-tune the trade-off between performance and complexity of their rules. For example, they can add something like `x-kubernetes-cel-cost-limit: 1000` in their CRD schema to indicate that they want to allow more expensive rules.

I agree this is the type of bug fix that is legitimate to make during beta. @jpbetz, when the size changes came in, did our existing size estimation test coverage notice this cost increased? If not, is there a systemic change we could make to exercise each type of estimation combination so we have visibility to any future changes.

> Hi @cici37, I agree that the changes in cel-go should not break the backward compatibility of CRD validation rules, especially for users who have already defined and deployed their custom resources using the previous version of Kubernetes.

Existing persisted CRD objects should continue to work as-is on upgrade, but the CEL rules and/or schema would be required to fit within fixed cost estimates before making future updates/changes to the CEL rules @cici37, there should be unit tests ensuring updates to a CRD that don't change CEL rules are allowed even if the existing CEL rules exceed cost estimates, but can you verify that is the case?

> One suggestion I have is to use a **version flag** for the CEL library, so that users can specify which version of cel-go they want to use for their CRD validation rules.

That's not workable, both from an implementation perspective and from a fragmentation perspective. We explicitly don't want to allow opting into loopholes / bugs in cost estimation that allow CRD authors to make API servers do excessive amounts of work.

> Another suggestion I have is to use a **cost limit** parameter for the CEL library, so that users can adjust the budget for their CRD validation rules. This way, they can fine-tune the trade-off between performance and complexity of their rules. For example, they can add something like `x-kubernetes-cel-cost-limit: 1000` in their CRD schema to indicate that they want to allow more expensive rules.

Similar to above, the responsibility for API server resource consumption lies with the kube-apiserver admin, not the CRD author, so exposing this in the API is not something I would expect.
/assign

Thank you!

I guess the next step would be:
1. Audit the existing test suite regarding with the cel cost evaluation. Add estimated cost tests for every single operation, function, type, etc if it's not existing now.
2. Ensure updates to a CRD that don't change CEL rules are allowed even if the existing CEL rules exceed cost estimates. Currently it is not working like this but [CRD Validation Ratcheting](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4008) would definitely help here. cc @alexzielenski , please correct me if I'm wrong :)

Those should be done before the feature goes to GA. I am not sure about the policy of a GA feature relying on alpha/beta feature is acceptable or not.  [CRD Validation Ratcheting](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4008) is going to Beta in this release. The worst case is we have to wait further until the feature is ready.

> 2\. Currently it is not working like this but [CRD Validation Ratcheting](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4008) would definitely help here. cc @alexzielenski , please correct me if I'm wrong :)

I don't think that helps... CRD ratcheting is about validation of the custom resources. This is about validation of the CRD itself.

@liggitt thanks for clarifying! Are you suggesting while updating CRD, if the rules matching what's in the existing object, we should skip cost estimation check? That makes sense. I could start a PR if my understanding aligns :)

> @liggitt thanks for clarifying! Are you suggesting while updating CRD, if the rules matching what's in the existing object, we should skip cost estimation check? That makes sense. I could start a PR if my understanding aligns :)

*something* along those lines, though now that I think about it, other changes in the schema could affect the number of times a CEL expression could be run (dropping or increasing maxItems, maxProperties, etc)

we already collect preexisting expressions when updating a CRD in order to allow already-persisted expressions (possibly persisted via a newer API server) making use of new CEL features:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f19b62fc0914b38941922afefd1e34eb55f87ee7/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apis/apiextensions/validation/validation.go#L192

I think that is what I was thinking of.

I would probably focus on:
1. test coverage of the edges of the cost estimation so we don't pick up changes there without knowing
2. _possibly_ coarse-grained skipping of schema/cel validation for a particular version in a CRD for updates which don't change anything under that version's schema (would let someone make unrelated updates to the CRD and leave an existing version's schema / CEL rules alone)

Thank you! We have those work planned for the current cycle.
/assign
/assign @jiahuif

title: 1.28 kube-apiserver failed due to nil pointer panic when requests routed to "kube-aggregator"
body:
### What happened?

After control plane nodes recreation and after kube-apiserver being brought again. In some scenarios (we are still investigating the exact scenario), we found some request (mostly `GET openapi/v2`) may cause nil pointer panic in kube-apiserver:

```
I0919 05:56:20.096796       1 handler.go:153] kube-aggregator: GET "/openapi/v2" satisfied by nonGoRestful
I0919 05:56:20.096825       1 pathrecorder.go:241] kube-aggregator: "/openapi/v2" satisfied by exact match
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x0 pc=0x16bfbe0]

goroutine 8765 [running]:
k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached.(*Replaceable[...]).Get(0x5576440)
    vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached/cache.go:296 +0x60
k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached.(*listMerger[...]).prepareResultsLocked.func1()
    vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached/cache.go:188 +0x5f
created by k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached.(*listMerger[...]).prepareResultsLocked
    vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached/cache.go:182 +0x9b
```

And it seems to only happen when the request is routed to `kube-aggregator`, no similar issues on `kube-apiserver`, `apiextensions-apiserver`. Also `kube-aggregator` is able to back to normal eventually.

Based on the stack trace, we found in [below block](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.2/vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached/cache.go#L296) in `kube-openapi` that the `c.cache.Load()` could be nil which is causing this panic:

```
func (c *Replaceable[T]) Get() Result[T] {
	result := (*c.cache.Load()).Get()

	for {
		cResult := c.result.Load()
		if result.Err != nil && cResult != nil && cResult.Err == nil {
			return *cResult
		}
		if c.result.CompareAndSwap(cResult, &result) {
			return result
		}
	}
}
```



### What did you expect to happen?

Check cache is nil to avoid panic

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Still in investigation of why it happens and how to reproduce easily. 

Per the current resource we have, it may happen on a single control plane node cluster with DHCP IP setting. And after recreating the control plane node (IP of the machine is changed), the `kubectl apply` would fail due to this issue.

### Anything else we need to know?

We also found recently there is a big change in `kube-openapi` which is merged into the main branch, need to verify if the nil pointer issue has been handled:

* https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/pull/405/files
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/dad1b2a4306e925fb6e5cd93e5d651bfb2ccdf8b

### Kubernetes version

> Based on the stack trace, we found in [below block](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.2/vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached/cache.go#L296) in kube-openapi that the c.cache.Load() could be nil which is causing this panic:

Yeah, that shouldn't be a problem, we should never use that object uninitialized, so that a red-herring, but indicating that somewhere we are using the object uninitialized.

The code (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/controllers/openapi/aggregator/aggregator.go#L223-L226) creates an info without a spec, which is then supposed to be created in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/controllers/openapi/aggregator/aggregator.go#L230. Unfortunately we manage to use it in-between: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/controllers/openapi/aggregator/aggregator.go#L227C46-L227C66, which is wrong. The order of these is messed-up, we need to re-order so that we don't have the race-condition anymore.

/sig api-machinery
/triage accepted

title: `poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller` check blocks apiserver readiness for 1 minute if discovery cannot be completed
body:
### What happened?

I’m seeing some odd behavior with 1.28.2 that was not present in earlier releases, with regards to aggregated api services. It appears that the `poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller` is now blocking the apiserver from becoming ready for 1 minute, if discovery for an aggregated apiservice is not available when the apiserver is started. Note that this only happens if the apiservice is marked available when the apiserver is started; if it is unavailable at startup (Available status: false), or the service has no endpoints, the health check does not block and readyz returns `ok` without delay.

I am seeing this behavior in 1.28.1 and 1.28.2, but not v1.27.6 or v1.27.5

### What did you expect to happen?

apiserver becomes ready without any additional delays

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Deploy metrics-server to a Kubernetes cluster
2. Wait for api registration for `v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io` to complete (Available status is `true`).
3. Kill the kubelet and pods on the node hosting the metrics-server pod, such that the metrics-server service continues to show available endpoints, but the endpoint is not reachable.
4. Restart the apiserver before the `v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io` apiservice is marked unavailable
5. Note that the `poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller` check blocks readiness for 1 minute. After 1 minute the Available status is updated to `false`, and the health check passes.

### Anything else we need to know?

Other notes:
* Does not appear to make any difference if `AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint` feature-gate is set to false.
* If the metrics-server service has no endpoints available, the apiservice status reason is updated to `MisssingEndpoints` and the check passes quickly.
* If there is an available endpoint, but it is not reachable, the check seems to be stuck retrying the endpoint, with the following message repeated in the logs:
    `Sep 18 20:37:01 systemd-node-1 k3s[8000]: E0918 20:37:01.403911    8000 available_controller.go:460] v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io failed with: failing or missing response from https://10.42.0.2:10250/apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1: Get "https://10.42.0.2:10250/apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1": net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)`


Odd error from GC that I don't remember seeing in the past:
`Sep 18 20:34:30 systemd-node-1 k3s[7903]: I0918 20:34:30.744555    7903 garbagecollector.go:816] "failed to discover some groups" groups="<internal error: json: unsupported type: map[schema.GroupVersion]error>"`

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
systemd-node-1:/ # kubectl version
Client Version: v1.28.2+k3s-416d7e87
Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3
Server Version: v1.28.2+k3s-416d7e87
```

nodes.body: /sig api-machinery
cc @tnqn @Jefftree @apelisse

I investigated the cause of the delay and think it may be related to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118212 instead of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120108.

The following is where the 1 minute is delayed:
func (c *APIServiceRegistrationController) Run(stopCh <-chan struct{}, handlerSyncedCh chan<- struct{}) 
-> c.apiHandlerManager.AddAPIService(s)
--> s.openAPIAggregationController.AddAPIService(proxyHandler, apiService)
---> c.openAPIAggregationManager.AddUpdateAPIService(apiService, handler)
----> s.updateServiceLocked(apiService.Name)
-----> specInfo.downloader.Get()
------> d.downloader.Download(d.handler, d.etag)
-------> handler = http.TimeoutHandler(handler, specDownloadTimeout, "request timed out") // specDownloadTimeout is 1 * time.Minute
-------> handler.ServeHTTP(writer, req)
--------> if !handlingInfo.serviceAvailable {      // serviceAvailable is true according to the condition in APIService

Because the APIService is available in its status, it will try to get the v2 spec with a timeout of 1 minute. This also explains why there is no delay when the APIService is not available in its status.

The issue occurs only after v1.28 may be because https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118212 changed `c.openAPIAggregationManager.AddUpdateAPIService` to download the latest spec synchronously?
/triage accepted
/assign

title: kubelet: lookup node address logic for external provider assign wrong PodIPs to hostNetwork pods
body:
The kubelet  logic used to get the Node addresses when using an external provider, temporary assigns an address discovered from the node , this address can be overriden later by the external cloud provider

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0241da314e0e69817d66313b45a69c19d1ce7327/pkg/kubelet/nodestatus/setters.go#L123-L131


This was implemented in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/75229 to improve the  bootstrapping problems with some external cloud providers

The side effect of this behavior is that if the external cloud provider sets a different address/es, then the pods with `HostNetwork: true` will be showing the "first" addresses as their `PodIPs`, since we don't mutate those IPs once set to avoid problems

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0241da314e0e69817d66313b45a69c19d1ce7327/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1770-L1786

I think that we should revert the existing logic for external cloud providers, since is causing a temporary and inconsistent state and it seem to address mainly a problem with kubeadm https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/75229#issuecomment-516592142 but kubeadm folks seems to not need this functionality https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/75229#issuecomment-516580449

Announced mailing list https://groups.google.com/g/kubernetes-sig-cloud-provider/c/u8DH2hNY_FI/m/arryQvlzAQAJ

/kind bug
/sig network
/sig node

nodes.body:
/assign @andrewsykim @danwinship
/cc @thockin

>  since is causing a temporary and inconsistent state

So we don't want the external provider to update the IP of the node, right? But I think even if it updates the address, for pods with hostnetwork, it still gets the first address from nodeStatus as podIPs, why is it inconsistent?

> So we don't want the external provider to update the IP

the contrary, we don't want to shortcut the address assignment, if cloud provider is external the node should wait for the cloud provider to assign the address.

Let me put an example,  a node with IPs 10.0.0.1 and 2001:db2::3 and cloud-provider external that sets the IPv6 address first.

Right, now, the Node will use prefer IPv4 when it starts and assign the IP 10.0.0.1 to the node, hostNetwork pods will get that IP. and later the cloud provider will override the IPs and sets 2001:db2::3 as the address, so new hostNetwork pods will use the IPv6 address but old hostNetwork pods will have 10.0.0.1
I see, Now I think it makes sense, but we need to confirm that kubeadm really doesn't need it anymore.

> I see, Now I think it makes sense, but we need to confirm that kubeadm really doesn't need it anymore.

@neolit123 ^^^

> I think that we should revert the existing logic for external cloud providers, since is causing a temporary and inconsistent state and it seem to address mainly a problem with kubeadm

I don't know the history of why it works the way it currently does, but I agree that it's weird and seems likely to lead to problems, so if it turns out it's not necessary, then let's change it.

> The side effect of this behavior is that if the external cloud provider sets a different address/es, then the pods with HostNetwork: true will be showing the "first" addresses as their PodIPs, since we don't mutate those IPs once set to avoid problems

This is why we taint nodes initially and only remove the taint once cloud provider has initialized the node. So this is reallly an issue for pods tolerating this taint

> > I see, Now I think it makes sense, but we need to confirm that kubeadm really doesn't need it anymore.
> 
> @neolit123 ^^^

i don't understand what is being asked exactly, but if the Q is again whether kubeadm supports self-hosted control plane components in a DS, then no.

kubeadm does support the --cloud-privider=external on paper, but we don't have tests. i don't think we want to maintain them either.

@pacoxu do you have context?

For current behavior, the workaround would be `to delete hostNetwork:true pods and wait for recreation` if I understand correctly.

I don't know if there are any cloud provider installers that depend on this behavior. I prefer to fix the weird behavior to avoid potential problems. Or a problem detector has to cover this to check if a hostNet pod is not using the correct node IP.

> This is why we taint nodes initially and only remove the taint once cloud provider has initialized the node. So this is reallly an issue for pods tolerating this taint

yeah, but I think that is fair to give those pods the responsibility to deal with the known behavior (node will not have addresses until cloud provider external initializes) , than make the kubelet have two different addresses during its lifetime (that we discussed extensively https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/108281 and  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93898) We discarded this behavior because most components,  apps and features like downward API depend on the existing behavior of not changing the original IP 

For the temporal status without addresses we can just set the node as notReady https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120727

> For the temporal status without addresses we can just set the node as notReady https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120727

NetworkUnavailable might be more appropriate, but overall makes sense I think

@aojea is there a reported issue or bug that is reproducible based on what you describe in the isuse description? Logically what you said makes sense but I'm wondering how common the problem actually is
Ah, is it just https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120727 or are there others?
Oh -- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120727 is not even related, because they are not setting --cloud-provider=external

> @aojea is there a reported issue or bug that is reproducible based on what you describe in the isuse description? Logically what you said makes sense but I'm wondering how common the problem actually is

yeah, @andrewsykim I opened this issue because when I tried to bring up an IPv6 only cluster with kops in GCE it failed and one of the problems was that the hostNetwork pods were using IPv4 as pod ips ... is not likely anybody hits this with IPv4 or dual stack, since cloud-provider and kubelet will agree most of the times, but as soon that you use IPv6 only or IPv6 primary you ends with this problem

> because when I tried to bring up an IPv6 only cluster with kops in GCE it failed and one of the problems was that the hostNetwork pods were using IPv4 as pod ips

Isn't this a configuration issue on the kubelet and not with external cloud providers then? You should configure kubelet to bootstrap initially with an IPv6 address and not IPv4.

> Isn't this a configuration issue on the kubelet and not with external cloud providers then? You should configure kubelet to bootstrap initially with an IPv6 address and not IPv4.

Still does not work for dual-stack, or if there are multiple addresses on the node, or multiple interfaces ....

I don't see the reason why kubelet should configure the node addresses in the first place just to wait for the cloud-provider to override that ... the pods bootstrap problem is another thing, kubelet should not be ready if there are no addresses in the node https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120753, but current behavior is compensating the problem of having an external  source for the address allocation, that is clearly not generalizable

>yeah, @andrewsykim I opened this issue because when I tried to bring up an IPv6 only cluster with kops in GCE it failed and one of the problems was that the hostNetwork pods were using IPv4 as pod ips ... is not likely anybody hits this with IPv4 or dual stack, since cloud-provider and kubelet will agree most of the times, but as soon that you use IPv6 only or IPv6 primary you ends with this problem

For cloud-provider-vsphere, what we did to workaround is to identify the preferred ip address to get, which interface, which rank, then in bootstrap time we get it and pass it to kubelet flag `--node-ip`. Now `--node-ip` support dual stack address with external cloud-provider. 

Without the kubelet starting node with some IP, if there is issue in CPI code or in the config, then it would be hard for us to debug CPI since getting the log will getting error that node doesn't have prefered ip. Might need to get the container log from containerd directly by ssh into the node.

> kubelet should not be ready if there are no addresses in the node 

You mentioned this is for GCE, I remember @jayunit100 brought it up in here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120486 that now the `NodeNetworkUnavailable` is also [managed by CCM](https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider/blob/73ce03d745d168cd8169b5f9ebfde4120b9ca82f/controllers/route/route_controller.go#L398) if CCM has route controller enable, which doesn't have clear ownership between CMM and CNI which should reconcile it. And according to the CCM logic [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider/blob/master/controllers/node/node_controller.go#L458-L470), in GCE case it will managed the `NodeNetworkUnavailable` in CCM, and probably will mark it as false once the route is ready, then node could possibly becomes ready.
So maybe that's why in your case the node becomes ready even though the node doesn't have the address you preferred.

> You mentioned this is for GCE

I found it trying with GCE, but  that is not important, I can hit this with Openshift or Rancher or Kind ... my goal is to define a general behavior of the kubelet that is consistent and easier to think about, without breaking anyone of course, but current implementation is a footgun and seems tailor made... do we enforce all cloud providers to pass the --node-ip flag to kubelet to match their IPs?  🤷  I will put this for the next sig-network agenda so we can go deeper and talk more about it
Another example of this problem in Azure and CAPG @lubronzhan @andrewsykim https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116879

> NetworkUnavailable might be more appropriate, but overall makes sense I think

> jayunit100 brought it up in here #120486 that now the NodeNetworkUnavailable is also managed by CCM if CCM has route controller enable, which doesn't have clear ownership between CMM and CNI which should reconcile it.

Yeah, the NetworkUnavailable condition/taint is not extensible or reusable. Any change to its current semantics will not work correctly in some environments.

Ohk we ran into similar issue today, We didn't pass --node-ips to kubelet, and we are setting ipv6 as primary ipfamily, but kubelet chose ipv4 address at the beginning, so all hostNetwork pod has ipv4 address. Now even after CPI has fixed the node ip to put ipv6 address as primary address, all following pods still has ipv4 addresses regardless. Example:
```
kubo@l4pG6sGMZI8mF:~$ kubectl get po -o wide -A | grep cluster-a-control-plane-flvz4
default                multi-nic-pod-macvlan-l2qpj                              1/1     Running     0               8m55s   100.96.0.28                         cluster-a-control-plane-flvz4         <none>           <none>
kube-system            antrea-agent-kbtld                                       2/2     Running     0               2d11h   10.168.220.178                      cluster-a-control-plane-flvz4         <none>           <none>
kube-system            antrea-controller-74b5f7848c-74rvn                       1/1     Running     0               2d11h   10.168.220.178                      cluster-a-control-plane-flvz4         <none>           <none>
kube-system            coredns-7b7646b589-b7zvr                                 1/1     Running     0               2d11h   100.96.0.4                          cluster-a-control-plane-flvz4
```

Node addresses:
```
status:
  addresses:
  - address: cluster-a-control-plane-flvz4
    type: Hostname
  - address: fd01:0:106:209:250:56ff:fe9a:17ae
    type: InternalIP
  - address: 10.168.220.178
    type: InternalIP
  - address: fd01:0:106:209:250:56ff:fe9a:17ae
    type: ExternalIP
  - address: 10.168.220.178
    type: ExternalIP
```
so @lubronzhan , does it mean you agree we need to fix this as in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120751?

I'm in favor of removing the behavior to bootstrap initial addresses as long as we are confident it is not breaking some exitsing behavior that some provider is depending on. 

I still find the scenario in [comment#](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120720#issuecomment-1731901005) a little odd, those pods should not be running on the node if the CCM has no initialized them yet. I wonder if the actual problem here is that node addresses are only updated after the first initialization: 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c5cf0ac1889f55ab51749798bec684aed876709d/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/node/node_controller.go#L498-L500

Which means pods can be admitted between the time time the cloud provider taint is removed and when addresses are updated.

>so @lubronzhan , does it mean you agree we need to fix this as in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120751?

At least from cloud-provider-vsphere it shouldn't depend on this behavior to bootstrap. It's just that it would be harder for people to debug the CPI issue or issues in other component that comes before CPI like KCM/kube-apiserver/etcd in the future if something goes wrong before CPI could initialize the node. Example issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-vsphere/issues/299

>I still find the scenario in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120720#issuecomment-1731901005 a little odd, those pods should not be running on the node if the CCM has no initialized them yet.

Yeah this is weird. For pod like apiserver pod has ipv4 address, which make sense since it comes before CPI. Kubelet could choose the wrong IP at the beginning
```
kube-system            kube-apiserver-cluster-a-control-plane-flvz4             1/1     Running     0                3d21h   10.168.220.178                      cluster-a-control-plane-flvz4         <none>           <none>
```
now CPI already removes the taints and updated the node with correct IP address, also the node has correct podCIDRs, with ipv6 address at the front.
```
spec:
  podCIDR: fd00:100:96::/64
  podCIDRs:
  - fd00:100:96::/64
  - 100.96.0.0/24
```
Still if I create a new pod on that node, it will be assigned with a ipv4 address as primary ip. 
For example that `multi-nic-pod-macvlan-l2qpj` test pod was created long after the CPI initialized the node.
```
default                multi-nic-pod-macvlan-l2qpj                              1/1     Running     0               8m55s   100.96.0.28                         cluster-a-control-plane-flvz4         <none>           <none>
```

```
  hostIP: fd01:0:106:209:250:56ff:fe9a:17ae
  phase: Running
  podIP: 100.96.0.28
  podIPs:
  - ip: 100.96.0.28
  - ip: fd00:100:96::1c
```

And we only  experience issue with pod that get created on this node, all other pod on other node will have ipv6 address as primary address.

/triage accepted
/priority important-longterm
@lubronzhan that should not be a problem if having node addresses is a requirement of node readiness https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120753

The AWS EKS AMIs that we provide specify `--node-ip` which avoids this issue. If that flag is not passed, then the same problem exists along with a slightly worse one that we intend to fix, https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-aws/issues/656.

nodes.title: kubelet: cloud-provider external addresses
nodes.body:
Kubelet, when using cloud provider external, initializes temporary the node addresses using the --node-ip flag values if set, until the cloud provider overrides it.

This behavior has undesired consequences if the cloud-provider addresses are different than the original ones, specially for hostNetwork pods, that inherit these addresses from the Node.

Since some cloud-providers depend on this behavior, in order to keep backward compatibility, assume that the specifying addresses via the node-ip flags means that the intent is to keep the existing behavior to temporary initialize the addresses.

If the node-ips are the unspecified addresses or are not set, then wait for the external cloud provider to set the node addresses.

/kind bug
/kind documentation
/kind feature

Fixes #120720


```release-note
Kubelet, when using cloud provider external, initializes temporary the node addresses using the --node-ip flag values if set, until the cloud provider overrides it.
```

title: Pods are stuck ContainerCreating after volume detach error and KCM restart
body:
### What happened?

After KCM restart, any Pod that reuses a volume that failed to detach gets stuck ContainerCreating with message:

`
User "system:node:ip-10-0-243-205.us-east-2.compute.internal" cannot get resource "volumeattachments" in API group "storage.k8s.io" at the cluster scope: no relationship found between node 'ip-10-0-243-205.us-east-2.compute.internal' and this object
`

See steps to reproduce below, it's quite a complex condition. It happens when a pod is restarted, a CSI driver "busy" (i.e. times out) + KCM restarted at a wrong time.

### What did you expect to happen?

Pods start just fine.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?


1. Create a Pod that uses an attachable CSI volume.
2. Delete the Pod. Make sure it unmounts successfully, but any `ControllerUnpublish` fails with a transient error, such as timeout. The external attacher continues to detach the volume at this point.
3. Stop kube-controller-manager (KCM) and start a new one. Wait for any leader election etc - it's important for the new KCM to populate A/D controller with no pod using the detaching volume. Let the A/D controller to observe detach error.
4. Create a new Pod on the same node that uses the same volume.
5. Let the CSI driver to detach the volume (i.e. stop injecting any transient errors).

At this point:

- The external attacher succeeds detaching the volume, VolumeAttachment is deleted.
- The volume is marked as attached in node status (!!!) despite no VolumeAttachment exists. A/D controller does not even try to create a new VolumeAttachment, the volume is marked as attached in its Actual State of World (ASW).
- Kubelet tries to mount the volume, but WaitForAttach fails with: `cannot get resource "volumeattachments" in API group "storage.k8s.io" at the cluster scope: no relationship found between node '127.0.0.1' and this object`, basically forever.

I created [a script with a reproducer](https://people.redhat.com/jsafrane/detach-error/).

* The script expects that the cluster is created by `hack/local-up-cluster.sh`, because it restarts KCM in the middle.
* It uses my hacked hostpath CSI driver to inject detach errors. Sources are at https://github.com/jsafrane/csi-driver-host-path/tree/hack-detach-error / the last commit(s) there.

### Anything else we need to know?

There are two issues that together lead to this situation:

1. After `Detach()` fails, [A/D controller marks the volume as fully attached](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/887ac275a2cfb6030df80bbe3066609336fa220a/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L508-L511), i.e. puts it back to `node.status.volumesAttached`.
    * With the volume in `node.status.volumesAttached`, kubelet may try to mount it, while the external attacher tries to detach it. It is not as bad as it sounds, because kubelet can't read VolumeAttachment with the deletion timestamp and it will not call `NodeStage` / `NodePublish` of un-attached volume.
2. After KCM starts, all VolumeAttachments that don't have a Pod [are marked as Uncertain](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/887ac275a2cfb6030df80bbe3066609336fa220a/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/attach_detach_controller.go#L763-L763) (that's good), but also [as mounted on node](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/887ac275a2cfb6030df80bbe3066609336fa220a/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/cache/actual_state_of_world.go#L370-L370) (that's probably bad).
    * When the newly started KCM re-tries to detach the volume and gets an error again, it marks the volume as fully attached (same as the previous point) and adds it to `node.status.volumesAttached`.
    * Now the volume is both mounted + attached in ASW and A/D controller actually stops here and waits forever for kubelet to unmount the volume.


### Kubernetes version


title: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy: variable expression type not recognized as return type in expression that evaluates the variable
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Variables field is added to ValidatingAdmissionPolicy in 1.28. Currently the usage of variables would expect a operator associated. 
e.g. (thanks to Mariam Fahmy for raising the issue)
```
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: "chech-deployment-labels"
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   ["apps"]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations:  ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
      resources:   ["deployments"]
  variables:
    - name: environment
      expression: "has(object.metadata.labels) && 'env' in object.metadata.labels && object.metadata.labels['env'] == 'prod'"
  validations:
    - expression: "variables.environment"
      message: "Deployment labels must be env=prod"
```
Above will fail with error: 
```
The ValidatingAdmissionPolicy "chech-deployment-labels" is invalid: spec.validations[0].expression: Invalid value: "variables.environment": must evaluate to bool
```
Meanwhile the `- expression: "variables.environment == true"` will pass.

The reason is when variables be evaluated to non dyn type(like bool or string), it will require special handling(like casting) since we use dyn type everywhere. 

### Why is this needed?

It might confuse user.

Tests I'd expect to see verify this behavior:

- PASS: A variable is of type bool, an expression returns the variable
- PASS: A variable is of type string, a messageExpression returns the variable
- PASS: A variable is of type dyn, at runtime the dyn is a bool, an expression returns the variable
- PASS: A variable is of typedyn, at runtime the dyn is a string, an messageExpression returns the variable
- PASS: A expression is of type dyn, at runtime the dyn is of type bool
- PASS: A messageExpression is of type dyn, at runtime the dyn is of type string
- COMPILE ERROR: A variable is of type bool, an expression tries to perform a non-bool (e.g. string replace) operation on the variable, this should resultsin a compile error
- COMPILE ERROR: A variable is of type string, an expression tries to perform a non-string (e.g. less than) operation on the variable, this should result in a compile error
- RUNTIME ERROR: A variable is of type dyn, at runtime the dyn is a bool, an expression tries to perform a non-bool (e.g. string replace) operation on the variable, this should result in a runtime error

I'd also expect to see some cases covering variables of other types (maps, lists, duration, quantity, ...) to make sure we're over-fitting for bool and string.
/retitle ValidatingAdmissionPolicy: variable expression type not recognized as return type in expression that evaluates the variable
/assign @jiahuif

title: Kubernetes Docker Config Json Globbing Not As Documented
body:
### What happened?
K8s Docker config json globbing is not as documented for subdomain wildcarding.
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/credentialprovider/keyring.go

### Impact
The user impact is that people create `imagePullSecrets` and corresponding configuration to use private registries and the credentials do not get used leading to `4xx` with the registry, image pull errors and some confusion. 

### What did you expect to happen?

Docs indicate that host glob `*my-registry.io` would work to be used as auth for e.g
```
foo.my-registry.io
foo.bar.my-registry.io
```
* https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images/#config-json
* https://github.com/kubernetes/website/blob/main/content/en/docs/concepts/containers/images.md

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run package unit tests with the following cases added to `TestURLsMatch`:
```
		{
			globURL:       "*kubernetes.io",
			targetURL:     "foo.kubernetes.io",
			matchExpected: true,
		},
		{
			globURL:       "*kubernetes.io",
			targetURL:     "foo.bar.kubernetes.io",
			matchExpected: true,
		},
```

nodes.title: DRA: call plugins for claims even if exist in cache
nodes.body:
Initial PR to gather Feedback if the proposed approach for fixing #119850 is acceptable or a different approach is required.
See [Alternatives](#alternatives) section for a different approach.

<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/first-contribution.md#your-first-contribution and developer guide https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/development.md#development-guide
2. Please label this pull request according to what type of issue you are addressing, especially if this is a release targeted pull request. For reference on required PR/issue labels, read here:
https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-release/release.md#issuepr-kind-label
3. Ensure you have added or ran the appropriate tests for your PR: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-testing/testing.md

5. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests
-->

#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

<!--
Add one of the following kinds:
/kind bug
/kind cleanup
/kind documentation
/kind feature

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Today, DRA manager does not call plugin NodePrepareResource
for claims that it previously successfully handled, that is,
if claims are present in cache (checkpoint) even if node
rebooted.

After node reboots, it is required to call DRA plugin
for resource claims so that plugins may prepare them
again in case the resources dont persist reboot.

To achieve that, once kubelet is started, we call DRA
plugins for claims once if a pod sandbox is required
to be created during PodSync.

##### DRA Manager NodePrepareResource  in different scenarios:

When kubelet restarts, DRA Manager NodePrepareResource will not be called during SyncPod as pods will already be in running state (pod sandbox state ready), thus no redundant calls will be performed to DRA plugins.

When A Pod's sandbox need to be (re)created, DRA Manager NodePrepareResource will be called however its claims in in-memory claim cache would be marked as "prepared", thus no call to plugin will occur.

When Kubelet restarts AND a Pod's sandbox need to be (re)created, DRA manager will call DRA plugin. At that point its expected that the plugin is idempotent and return same results as resource already exists.

When Node reboots, resource may not be created on the node. however same steps as above will occur, which will trigger resource preparation by DRA plugin.
Note that result may be different in this case. thus latest results for a claim are stored in checkpoint. 

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #119850 

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:
Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
NONE

#### Alternatives

Place DRA manager checkpoint file under /var/run/kubelet so that its content is cleared
on node boot. that way if a pod sandbox is required to be created (during PodSync), NodePrepareResouce call will only
call DRA plugins for a given resource claim once.

```
  "requestURI": "/api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/pods?pretty=true&allowWatchBookmarks=false&labelSelector=<selector>&resourceVersion=862900435&watch=false",
  "verb": "list",
  "user": {

      "authentication.kubernetes.io/pod-name": [
        "<pod-name>"
```
